title: Edge ingress local buffer with loss-tolerant pushback and compact serialization
creator: Asha Raman
description: Introduce a small local-first buffering layer at the console edge to absorb short bursts from SDK clients, emit compact serialized records to the main ingest stream, and provide a configurable, loss-tolerant pushback mechanism per-tenant to avoid overload on downstream processors.
background: Current console telemetry ingress experiences tail latency spikes and occasional upstream backpressure cascades when many SDK clients burst (e.g., during customer CI runs or rollout sweeps). Existing solutions either drop events silently at the edge or backpressure TCP connections which harms client UX. We need an intermediate edge layer that smooths bursts, reduces tokenized record size over the wire, and provides explicit non-fatal pushback signals to clients that can retry or degrade fidelity.
proposed_solution: Build an edge service (EdgeBuffer) colocated in regional edge pools. EdgeBuffer will:
proposed_solution_steps: Accept incoming telemetry over existing HTTP/gRPC endpoints and immediately ack with an ingress token to avoid blocking critical paths
Store up to configurable per-tenant local buffer (in-memory + small SSD spill) with LRU eviction and tunable retention window
Emit compact, schema-driven binary serialized messages (CBOR-based with field dictionaries) to existing Kafka topic to reduce bandwidth and improve broker throughput
Expose a non-fatal pushback response (HTTP 429-with-retry-info or gRPC custom code) indicating degradation level and suggested client backoff/fidelity reduction
Provide observability: per-tenant buffer occupancy, spill events, serialization savings, and pushback rates to Console dashboards
Admin controls: per-tenant buffer caps, loss tolerance policy (drop-oldest, sample, drop-noncritical-fields), and emergency bypass to route to cold storage
tradeoffs: EdgeBuffer adds complexity and an additional operational surface area. Benefits: smoother downstream load, lower bandwidth cost, and improved client experience under burst. Downsides: potential for delayed visibility (small buffer retention), more work for schema migration of the compact serializer, and additional failure modes (edge spill, SSD wear). We mitigate by conservative defaults, metrics-driven rollouts, and automatic fail-open to existing direct ingest on edge failure.
acceptance_criteria: EdgeBuffer deployed to staging edge pool and receives production-like synthetic bursts without dropping >0.5% of critical events
Serialized message size reduced by >=35% for typical console metrics payloads compared to existing JSON pipeline
Downstream broker write throughput increased (measured as stable throughput with 20% fewer transient publish failures) under synthetic 2x burst workload
Clients receive pushback headers with retry guidance and SDK changes handle suggested fidelity fallback in at least one language SDK (node)
rollout_plan: 1) Implement EdgeBuffer prototype + compact serializer; unit tests and benchmark harness
2) Internal canary: deploy to a single edge region and enable for internal Redwood teams with monitoring and alerting
3) Gradual per-tenant opt-in (start with low-traffic tenants), collect metrics for 2 weeks, iterate on eviction and spill heuristics
4) Enable default for all new tenants; provide migration playbook for high-throughput tenants
5) Full production flip with SLA monitoring and automatic rollback on regressions
tests: Load test harness that simulates client bursts with configurable concurrency and payload shapes
Serializer fuzzing to validate forward/backward schema compatibility and malformed payload handling
Chaos tests: simulate SSD spills, sudden edge termination, and broker unavailability to assert fail-open behavior
E2E integration: verify SDK receives pushback, performs fidelity downgrade, and resumes normal flow after backoff
success_metrics: 95th percentile end-to-end ingest latency reduced under burst by >=25%
Total bandwidth to brokers reduced proportional to serialization improvement (target >=35%)
Rate of downstream throttling errors during bursts decreased by >=40%
Percentage of tenants using EdgeBuffer opt-in reaches 60% within 8 weeks of GA
